title: A Confirmatory Paired Evaluation of Generate→Verify→Repair vs LLM‑Only NetOps Suggestions: A Reproducible Ceiling/Null Result
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired study (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) that measures the marginal effect of a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipeline versus accepting an LLM suggestion directly for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Under the frozen contract (K=200 deterministically selected tasks; single shared generator candidate per task; requested_model = gpt-5-mini), both arms produced 200/200 validator‑compliant applies and the repair step was never invoked. Primary paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis H1 (that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing changes vs LLM‑only) was not supported under the tested sampling/model/validator regime. All execution, scoring, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived and hashed for deterministic replay (see Disclosure). We interpret this as a ceiling/null outcome specific to the registered contract and provide artifact‑grounded guidance for designing failure‑rich follow‑ups.

sections.introduction:
LLM‑assisted NetOps workflows commonly translate operator intent into device configurations. Operational safety demands that such translations avoid regressions (reachability loss, unintended service disruption). Architectures that couple a generator (LLM) with a deterministic verifier and an automated repair stage (generate→verify→repair, G→V→R) are widely advocated to bound risk. However, rigorous, preregistered, artifact‑archived causal evidence quantifying the verifier/repair marginal effect is scarce. We therefore preregistered a paired experiment to isolate that marginal effect under a conservative, reproducible contract.
Research question. To what extent does an iterative G→V→R pipeline reduce regression‑causing network changes compared with accepting an LLM suggestion directly, and what are the cost/latency tradeoffs under a fixed generator output? 
Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, deterministically selected paired evaluation (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) with complete artifact hashing; (2) a reproducible ceiling/null empirical outcome (both arms 200/200 validator‑compliant) together with the full artifact archive for independent replay; (3) artifact‑grounded recommendations for sampling, estimand, and closed‑loop design choices needed to reveal verifier value in future studies.
sections.related_work: Recent literature advocates generate–validate–repair and verifier‑assisted agentic NetOps to reduce hallucination and regressions (e.g., Cornetto and contemporaneous generate/verify/repair architectures). Prior benchmarks typically report model rankings or end‑to‑end success; operational questions require causal contrasts that estimate the isolated contribution of verification and repair machinery. Our work complements these lines by (i) preregistering a paired estimand to isolate verifier marginality, (ii) publishing bit‑verified execution and scoring traces, and (iii) reporting a reproducible ceiling/null outcome under a clearly specified contract. We position this run as an artifact‑grounded audit of the particular contract rather than a general condemnation of verifiers.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and frozen contract. The full preregistration (SHA‑256 = a6d73a5cc0bda22e691a3634068a881b36ae274a65ab33919a647ec32c56e622) fixed the paired design, deterministic sampling, generator/validator identities, and analysis plan prior to observing outcomes. Key frozen choices: paired binary estimator (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline); K=200 tasks deterministically selected from an assembled public pool by SHA‑256(intent_string) ascending after filtering to intents the preregistered deterministic validator reported as covered; a single shared_initial_generation per task (both arms used identical generator candidate) so the paired contrast isolates verifier+repair marginality; requested_model = gpt-5-mini; maximum_model_calls predeclared = 400; initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. The execution adapter was hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce92558ed...).
Task corpus and inclusion rule. To ensure meaningful validation, the preregistration required including only intents that the deterministic validator reported as covered. This inclusion rule reduces the prevalence of verifier rejections in the sample and therefore shifts the sampled regime toward validator‑covered cases (a design choice explicitly recorded in the preregistration and manifests).
Execution and artifact capture. Every prompt, response, provider call trace, per‑episode scoring JSON, and validator trace was captured and hashed. Representative artifact fingerprints (full manifest in Disclosure): execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...), execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce9255...), and per‑episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/*.json. Scoring JSONs embed validator diagnostics used for audit: normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, validation_before/after with simulated final_state snapshots.
Primary analysis. The preregistered primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The confirmatory test is an exact McNemar two‑sided test. Uncertainty was reported with a paired bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729). Analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1) and seeds are archived; analysis outputs and contingency table are in analysis/*.csv (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...).
Reproducibility guarantees. All artifacts required to deterministically replay selection, generation, validation, and analysis are archived and hashed in the execution manifest. The initial master prompt used by the autonomous researcher is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 reported in Disclosure).
sections.results:
Execution summary. The run completed as preregistered: planned episodes 400 (2 arms × 200 tasks); completed episodes 400; failed episodes 0; model calls used = 200 (one shared generator call per task); repair was never invoked (repair_applied=false in all scoring JSONs). Primary paired outcome. The paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...) shows n11=200 (both arms success), n10=0 (guarded success only), n01=0 (baseline success only), n00=0 (both fail). Observed marginal rates: baseline = 200/200 (100%); guarded = 200/200 (100%). Inferential statistics: paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. Representative per‑task diagnostics. Each scoring JSON records validator diagnostics (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 = 3055f874...), including difficulty metadata, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, and a final_state snapshot that records the validator’s simulated post‑apply result. Representative tasks and their archived scoring JSONs are included in the manuscript evidence bundle; the full set of per‑task scoring JSONs is archived under execution/scoring/*.json for deterministic aggregation.
Repair pathway accounting and cost. Because every shared_initial_candidate passed the deterministic validator, the automated repair pathway was never exercised and therefore did not contribute to changes in outcomes or to additional model calls. Model_call accounting: the model_call budget was consumed only by the shared_initial_generation stage (200 generator calls total), consistent with the preregistered adapter budget (maximum_model_calls = 400; model_calls_used = 200). 
Requested reviewer item (aggregated difficulty summary). The preregistered experiment did not compute an aggregated difficulty‑level distribution across the full K=200 sample during the main analysis pass; the per‑task difficulty labels are present in the archived scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json) and the task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl) and can be deterministically aggregated off‑line. We therefore do not report fabricated aggregate counts here. The archive locations and fingerprints are provided in the Disclosure to enable deterministic computation of difficulty counts (instructions: parse execution/scoring/*.json and count validation_before.difficulty.level values; file paths and hashes are in the execution manifest). (Rationale: preserving the preregistered analysis outputs and avoiding post hoc summaries that were not precomputed.)
Reproducibility pointers. Key artifact fingerprints (for deterministic replay and independent aggregation): execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4...), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...), execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = 1acce92558ed...), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5...), analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 1cb072b4db7c...), and the initial master prompt provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 in Disclosure).
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. Under the preregistered contract the G→V→R marginal effect was zero: the deterministic validator accepted every generator candidate and repairs were unnecessary. This ceiling/null result is artifact‑grounded and reproducible, but it is conditional on three conservative design choices that materially reduced the probability of validator failure in the sampled regime: (1) the inclusion rule explicitly filtered tasks to intents the validator reported as covered (this reduces observed verifier rejections), (2) the shared_initial_generation design fixed generator output across arms and therefore measured only verifier+repair marginality on fixed candidates rather than a closed‑loop, adaptive improvement, and (3) the single requested model (gpt-5-mini) and the particular deterministic validator implementation jointly determined the observed ceiling.
Implications for practice and follow‑ups. The ceiling outcome does not imply verifiers are unnecessary in production. To measure operational verifier value researchers should (i) sample failure‑rich distributions (historical incident corpora or adversarially constructed intents that exercise validator blind spots), (ii) adopt closed‑loop estimands that allow the generator to regenerate after validator failures (measuring end‑to‑end operational improvement), and (iii) evaluate across multiple generator strengths and alternative validator implementations. The archived artifacts support all these alternative analyses: per‑task scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/*.json) include difficulty labels and validator diagnostics needed to stratify or adversarially subsample; the task manifest and provider call traces permit deterministic replay of adaptive generator strategies.
Threats to validity. Internal validity: the paired shared_initial design isolates verifier marginality but precludes generator adaptation. Construct validity: the reported binary success depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; validator blind spots would undercount real regressions. External validity: single model, synthetic deterministic sampling filtered to validator coverage, and absence of adversarial sampling limit generalization. Conclusion validity: the degenerate contingency (all successes) yields trivial point estimate and CI; this correctly reflects the sampled regime and its low variance.
Operational recommendation. For operator‑oriented evaluations of G→V→R value, we recommend (a) deliberate inclusion of validator‑uncovered and adversarial intents in the confirmatory sample, (b) measuring closed‑loop end‑to‑end estimands (allow generator regeneration on validator failure), and (c) reporting per‑task validator diagnostics (parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration) alongside aggregated difficulty counts; all fields are present in the archived execution/scoring/*.json files for deterministic aggregation.
sections.conclusion: In a fully preregistered, deterministic paired evaluation (K=200 tasks selected deterministically from a validator‑covered pool; single shared_initial_generation per task; requested_model=gpt-5-mini), both baseline and guarded arms achieved 200/200 validator‑compliant applies. The preregistered confirmatory hypothesis H1 (that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing changes compared with accepting the LLM suggestion directly) was not supported under the tested sampling/model/validator regime (paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]). This ceiling/null result is reproducible from the archived artifacts (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6...; execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce9255...; provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 = 1872df1e...). It therefore motivates future artifact‑grounded evaluations that (i) sample failure‑rich intents, (ii) allow closed‑loop generator adaptation after validator feedback, and (iii) evaluate multiple generator strengths and validator implementations. All artifacts required to reproduce, reaggregate, or replay alternative estimands are archived and hashed to facilitate independent audit and exploration of verifier utility under alternative contracts. (Explicit restatement: the preregistered hypothesis H1 was not supported for the tested contract.)

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (requested_model = gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize to other LLMs without additional experiments.

Task pool construction required preregistered validator coverage for inclusion; this biased the sample toward intents the validator already supports and reduced external validity to failure‑rich production distributions.
Construct validity depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; validator blind spots would render the binary outcome an imperfect proxy for real operational regressions.

Shared_initial_generation fixes generator output across arms and prevents closed‑loop generator adaptation; the experiment therefore measures verifier marginality on fixed candidates rather than end‑to‑end adaptive improvement.
Observed ceiling (baseline success = 100%) made the preregistered power assumption inapplicable; inference is descriptive and bounded to the archived sampling/model regime.
